writeAppLogsToEfs.description:
Set to false (default) to stop fluent-bit from writing application logs to EFS.
Dynatrace now covers application-log observability, so the EFS copy fluent-bit
was writing is redundant/costly for SAAS/Axway-Managed deployments.
Customer-Managed on-prem deployments without Dynatrace should set this to true
to preserve current behavior (application logs continue to be written to EFS).
In fluent-bit DaemonSet mode, this flag ONLY gates the final EFS write performed
by handle_app_logs in configmap-luascript.yaml. Tailing and Kubernetes enrichment
of the built-in per-service application-log tags in configmap_daemonset.yaml
always happen, the same as transaction logs -- so these logs are still available
to any output plugin you configure via fluentBit.config.outputs regardless of
this flag's value; only the additional built-in EFS copy is skipped.
It has no effect on logFileEnabled's application-logger direct-write path,
no effect at all when fluentBit.enabled is false, and no effect on fluent-bit
Deployment mode (fluentBit.kind: Deployment), which still tails whatever
app-log files exist under the EFS root (a graceful no-op once writes stop,
per the chart's existing Ignore_Older/missing-file tailing behavior).
writeAppLogsToEfs.title: writeAppLogsToEfs

ocsp_cache_ttl.description:
Ceiling on how long a cached OCSP verdict stays usable, for the Certificates component's Validate
Certificate action. Accepts "Nms", "Ns" or bare milliseconds.
An entry expires at the EARLIER of the OCSP response's nextUpdate and this value, so lowering it
shortens every entry — including those from a responder that supplies its own nextUpdate. Raising
it never extends an entry past the responder's nextUpdate.
Deliberately separate from pepServer.ocspCacheTTL: that cache covers the mTLS front door, one
bounded client set shared across all tenants, while this one is per tenant and per mode over
arbitrary user-supplied certificates, so its key space is unbounded. The two need independent
tuning. Keep in step with EnvironmentProperty.ocsp_cache_ttl, which carries the same default for
non-Helm contexts such as tests.
0 and negative values are NOT a disable switch: they are rejected, and the orchestrator logs a
warning and falls back to the 86400s default. To make caching effectively inert, set a minimal
positive value such as "1ms" — each entry is then written and immediately expired.
ocsp_cache_ttl.title: ocsp_cache_ttl

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description:
The sink-agent is a consumer (no inbound HTTP traffic via Service/Ingress); quarkus.shutdown.delay
is hardcoded to 0 in application.properties so the ShutdownEvent fires immediately on SIGTERM.
The drain budget for in-flight jobs at shutdown is:
  drainBudget = terminationGracePeriodSeconds - 10s (Quarkus internal reserve)
This budget covers the parallel job drain (audit + purge schedulers). It is set high (1h) as a
ceiling so a large backlog of in-flight audit/purge work can drain fully before the pod is killed.
The budget is an upper bound, not a fixed wait: the graceful-shutdown scheduler returns as soon as
the in-flight jobs actually finish, so a normal shutdown (jobs idle or quick) terminates promptly
and does not consume the full 1h.
Hard floor: must be > 10s — at <= 10s the drain is bypassed entirely (executorService.shutdownNow()).
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds

  STRICT   - TLS, validates CA certificate and hostname (standard production TLS)
  MTLS     - mutual TLS via SPIRE; falls back to STRICT when SPIRE is not active
Leave empty to auto-select: MTLS when SPIRE is enabled, NONE otherwise

#      Failover Controller         ##
#####################################
Sub-quorum failover assistance for the internal Valkey above. Scoped under valkey.internal
since the controller STONITHs pods in its own namespace, so it can only ever manage

secondOpinionLeaseName.description: Dedicated Lease for the leader/standby second-opinion handshake - kept apart from the two above so that traffic never shares a write surface.
secondOpinionLeaseName.title: secondOpinionLeaseName

signalLeaseName.description: Carries the fence-heartbeat/graceful-shutdown annotations; leaseName above is used only by fabric8's LeaderElector.
signalLeaseName.title: signalLeaseName

livenessProbe.description:
Probes run on the plain, unauthenticated Quarkus management port (9000), which is the
only port the controller publishes.
livenessProbe.title: livenessProbe

nodeSelector.description:
Same requirement as valkey.internal.affinity above: controller pods should run on their
own dedicated nodes, and no two replicas should ever share a node - the controller only
deploys in a real HA topology (>=2 nodes), so losing one node must never take out both
replicas at once. Left empty since taints/labels are customer-specific: use
nodeSelector/tolerations to target your dedicated nodes, and uncomment (or adapt) the
required podAntiAffinity below to enforce one-pod-per-node.
nodeSelector.title: nodeSelector

podDisruptionBudget.description:
Protects the controller's 2-replica HA during voluntary disruptions (node drain,
upgrade) - without this both replicas could be evicted at once, losing all failover
coverage. minPods:1 keeps at least one replica (and leader election) available.
podDisruptionBudget.title: podDisruptionBudget

primaryHealthCheck.description:
Single source of truth for PrimaryHealthMonitor's cadence/threshold and the primary's
self-fencing grace period (fenceGraceSeconds) - these used to drift apart, now derive
from one block. fenceSafetyMarginSeconds lives here (same timing budget) even though
lease-watchdog.sh, not the controller, consumes it.

fenceHeartbeatStaleThresholdSeconds.description:
Bound (seconds) within which the master watchdog's Lease heartbeat
annotation (lease-watchdog.sh) is considered live; ~5x the watchdog's 2s loop interval.
fenceHeartbeatStaleThresholdSeconds.title: fenceHeartbeatStaleThresholdSeconds

gracefulShutdownStaleThresholdSeconds.description:
Bound (seconds) within which pre-stop.sh's graceful-shutdown signal
(Lease annotation) is considered fresh enough to fast-track a coordinated CLUSTER
FAILOVER; a few multiples of intervalSeconds so it survives at least one missed tick.
gracefulShutdownStaleThresholdSeconds.title: gracefulShutdownStaleThresholdSeconds

maxReplicaVetoCycles.description:
Cap on consecutive cycles a replica's own INFO replication self-report may veto
STONITH for the same primary - master_link_status is self-reported, so an uncapped
veto lets a compromised/stale replica block failover of a genuinely dead primary
forever. Once spent, the controller logs loudly and proceeds to STONITH anyway.
maxReplicaVetoCycles.title: maxReplicaVetoCycles

secondOpinionFreshnessThresholdSeconds.description:
How fresh a replica's reported master-link age must be to confirm the primary is
still live. Kept no higher than this block's own detection window (unhealthyThreshold
x intervalSeconds, ~15s) and well below Valkey's repl-timeout default of 60s.
secondOpinionFreshnessThresholdSeconds.title: secondOpinionFreshnessThresholdSeconds

secondOpinionRequestTimeoutSeconds.description:
Bound (seconds) the leader polls for a standby controller's cross-controller
second-opinion response before giving up and proceeding to STONITH; independent of
stonithConfirmTimeoutSeconds above.
secondOpinionRequestTimeoutSeconds.title: secondOpinionRequestTimeoutSeconds

stonithConfirmTimeoutSeconds.description:
Bounded poll timeout PrimaryHealthMonitor waits, after force-deleting the old primary's
pod (STONITH), for it to stop answering PING before proceeding to TAKEOVER anyway. Kept
short (STONITH is a fast, decisive action, not a crash-detection backstop).
stonithConfirmTimeoutSeconds.title: stonithConfirmTimeoutSeconds

primaryHealthCheck.title: primaryHealthCheck

terminationDrainSeconds.description:
Bounded wait for one in-flight tick to finish before the mTLS identity source closes
(termination.controller.check-primary.drain.secs - deliberately shorter than a
worst-case STONITH tick; see the budget note in application.properties).
terminationDrainSeconds.title: terminationDrainSeconds

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description:
Ceiling for ControllerShutdownHandler's whole drain. Must be >= (2 x
terminationDrainSeconds) + a 10s Quarkus shutdown reserve, since the handler applies
that drain twice sequentially (an in-flight checkPrimary() tick, then a second-opinion
response) after releasing the Lease - the default Kubernetes grace period let the
kubelet SIGKILL mid-close otherwise. 60 leaves headroom above the ~30s worst case.
terminationGracePeriodSeconds.title: terminationGracePeriodSeconds

failoverController.title: failoverController

gracefulHandoffTimeoutSeconds.description:
How long pre-stop.sh's wait_for_graceful_handoff() waits for this node to actually stop
being master before giving up and continuing shutdown anyway. Needed because a CLUSTER
FAILOVER's OK response only means the request was accepted, not that the (asynchronous)
handoff completed. Only relevant when subQuorumFailoverRequired.
gracefulHandoffTimeoutSeconds.title: gracefulHandoffTimeoutSeconds

maxMemoryPolicy.description: Will return errors when memory limit reached instead of evicting keys
maxMemoryPolicy.title: maxMemoryPolicy

enabled.description:
Operator-facing off switch for the whole /q/metrics listener (socat
never starts). Set to false if nothing scrapes this endpoint, to
remove it entirely rather than leave it reachable.

This endpoint computes its response fresh on every request - one
`valkey-cli info` call plus one `df` call, with no cached value ever
served - so freshness/correctness is never in question. DoS
resistance instead comes from: socat's `max-children=2` (concurrent
handler cap), the handler's `read -r -t 5` request-line timeout, this
`enabled` kill-switch, and the opt-in Calico `prometheusRule` netpol
above.
enabled.title: enabled

minReadySeconds.description:
How long a newly-rolled Valkey pod must stay Ready before the rollout advances - guards
against a crash-looping image taking out the last node. Only rendered for sub-quorum
topologies; native-quorum keeps its existing rollout pacing.
minReadySeconds.title: minReadySeconds

minReplicasMaxLagSeconds.description:
How stale (seconds) a replica's ACK may be before it stops counting toward Valkey's own
min-replicas-to-write write-fence - a data-plane self-fence, independent of the
controller's Kubernetes-based STONITH. Only takes effect when subQuorumFailoverRequired;
default 10 matches Valkey's own min-replicas-max-lag default, not derived from
primaryHealthCheck.* (a different timing budget - replication lag vs. detection).
minReplicasMaxLagSeconds.title: minReplicasMaxLagSeconds

nodeSelector.description:
Valkey pods should run on their own dedicated nodes, and no two Valkey pods should ever
share a node - losing one node must never be able to take out more than one replica.
Left empty here since the actual taints/labels are customer-specific: use
nodeSelector/tolerations to target your dedicated Valkey nodes, and uncomment (or adapt)
the required podAntiAffinity below to enforce the one-pod-per-node rule.
nodeSelector.title: nodeSelector

appendonly.description: Append-only file logging is on for durability - set to "no" to disable
appendonly.title: appendonly

claimTemplateAccessModes.description: claimTemplateAccessModes access mode for claim template
claimTemplateAccessModes.title: claimTemplateAccessModes

claimTemplateName.description: claimTemplateName name of the claim for valkey storage
claimTemplateName.title: claimTemplateName

claimTemplateRequestStorage.description: claimTemplateRequestStorage storage request size for the claim template
claimTemplateRequestStorage.title: claimTemplateRequestStorage

claimTemplateStorageClass.description:
claimTemplateStorageClass class that will dynamically create storage on desired cloud platform
For AWS set this value to gp3
For Azure set this value to managed-csi
claimTemplateStorageClass.title: claimTemplateStorageClass

logRotate.description: Log Rotation configuration for the Valkey log-rotation CronJob

frequency.description: How often to check whether the log needs rotating.
frequency.title: frequency

size.description: Minimum size of the log file before it gets rotated
size.title: size

RDB snapshotting configuration
Don't define or set rdbSnapshots to empty array [] to disable RDB snapshots entirely
Each entry defines: save after X seconds if at least Y keys changed
rdbSnapshots.title: rdbSnapshots

preexisting.description: Use preexisting: true if you want to use a preexisting service account (e.g. created by the infra)
preexisting.title: preexisting

zerotrust.description:
################################################
Zero-trust activation
################################################
Zero-trust is gated by `zerotrust.enabled`. When true, the chart deploys the configured
identity provider and injects workload-identity material into the dataplane components.

enabled.description: If true, activate zero-trust and deploy the configured identity provider for the data plane components.
enabled.title: enabled

managedLabel.description:
managedLabel is the Kubernetes label key stamped on every dataplane Pod managed by the
active zero-trust provider.
managedLabel.title: managedLabel

providers.description:
###############################################
#  Provider-specific configuration          ##
###############################################
Configuration consumed by the provider selected via `zerotrust.provider`.

enabled.description: If true, deploy a Calico NetworkPolicy for spire-agent. Requires the Calico CNI to be installed.
enabled.title: enabled

outboundRule.description:
outboundRule: destination rule for traffic to spire-server (ports 8081 gRPC and 8080 health).
DNS (port 53) and the Kubernetes API are always allowed and do not need to be included here.
Example for a ClusterIP service (CIDR covering the cluster service range):
  outboundRule:
    nets:
      - 10.96.0.0/12   # cluster service CIDR containing the spire-server ClusterIP
outboundRule.title: outboundRule

hostPath.description:
hostPath on the node to the CA cert that signed the kubelet serving certificate.
Only used when type is "hostCert".
hostPath.title: hostPath

type.description: How spire-agent verifies the kubelet TLS certificate. apiServerCA for EKS/GKE/AKS, hostCert for RKE2/k3s, skip not recommended.
type.title: type

commonName.description: Common Name for SPIRE server CA
commonName.title: commonName

clusterName.description: Must be unique per cluster to prevent identity collisions.
clusterName.title: clusterName

dataplaneLabel.description:
dataplaneLabel is the Kubernetes label key stamped on dataplane namespaces and read by the
spire-registrar to discover which namespaces to watch. Both the namespace hook and the
registrar sidecar use this value — changing it here keeps them in sync.
dataplaneLabel.title: dataplaneLabel

labelNamespaceHook.description:
labelNamespaceHook controls whether a pre-install Job is deployed to label the dataplane
namespace with <dataplaneLabel>=true. Set to false on clusters where the hook
pod cannot reach the Kubernetes API server (e.g. EKS with strict Gatekeeper/network policies).
When disabled, label the namespace manually before install:
  kubectl label namespace <namespace> <dataplaneLabel>=true --overwrite

enabled.description:
Enable on clusters with Calico global network policies that block hook pod egress
(e.g. EKS with restrictive Calico policies). Allows hook pod to reach the Kubernetes API server.
enabled.title: enabled

labelNamespaceHook.title: labelNamespaceHook

namespace.description:
namespace is the Kubernetes namespace where SPIRE server and agent resources are installed.
All dataplanes in the same cluster share this single SPIRE installation.
namespace.title: namespace

preexisting.description: If true, skip creating SPIRE resources — they already exist from a prior dataplane install in this cluster.
preexisting.title: preexisting

agentSvidTTL.description: TTL for spire-agent's own node SVID (default_x509_svid_ttl). Governs how long the agent can keep operating on a cached credential while spire-server is unreachable — keep this comfortably longer than any expected spire-server outage or rolling-upgrade window. Also the fallback TTL for workload entries when registrar.workloadSvidTTL is unset. Only minute/hour Go-duration units are accepted, and the value must be greater than zero.
agentSvidTTL.title: agentSvidTTL

bundleConfigMapName.description:
bundleConfigMapName is the ConfigMap the k8sbundle notifier writes the SPIRE CA bundle into.
The agent mounts this ConfigMap as its trust anchor (trust_bundle_path).
bundleConfigMapName.title: bundleConfigMapName

caTTL.description: Intermediate CA TTL for the SPIRE server. Only minute/hour Go-duration units are accepted, and the value must be greater than zero.
caTTL.title: caTTL

enabled.description: If true, deploy a Calico NetworkPolicy for spire-server. Requires the Calico CNI to be installed.
enabled.title: enabled

inboundRule.description:
inboundRule: source rule for spire-agent traffic on port 8081.
IMPORTANT: spire-agent uses hostNetwork:true — connections arrive from the NODE IP, not the
pod IP. A pod selector won't work. Use a net (CIDR) covering the cluster node IP range.
Example:
  inboundRule:
    nets:
      - 10.0.0.0/16    # VPC CIDR containing all cluster nodes
inboundRule.title: inboundRule

outboundRule.description:
outboundRule: optional destination rule for external egress (e.g. AWS KMS endpoint).
DNS (port 53) and the Kubernetes API are always allowed and do not need to be included here.
Example for AWS KMS:
  outboundRule:
    nets:
      - 0.0.0.0/0      # or narrow to kms.<region>.amazonaws.com IP ranges
outboundRule.title: outboundRule

type.description: How spire-server tracks its KMS key. file lets SPIRE create and manage the key; value references a pre-existing key ARN or alias.

value.description: KMS key ARN or alias. Required when keyIdentifier.type is value; ignored when file.

type.description: How spire-server stores its CA private key. disk for dev/RKE2, aws for EKS production, memory for ephemeral use with UpstreamAuthority.

healthPort.description:
healthPort: the port on which the registrar exposes /live and /ready probes.
Must not conflict with spire-server ports (8080 healthz, 8081 gRPC).
healthPort.title: healthPort

informerSyncTimeoutSeconds.description:
informerSyncTimeoutSeconds: how long (in seconds) the registrar waits for the Kubernetes
namespace or pod informer to complete its initial LIST sync before falling back to a
direct API call (for namespace informer) or continuing with a WARN (for pod informer).
Must be > 0. Default 60s accommodates cold JVM startup (TLS handshake + classloading).
informerSyncTimeoutSeconds.title: informerSyncTimeoutSeconds

initialDelaySeconds.description:
initialDelaySeconds: startup grace period (seconds) before the registrar's
liveness probe begins evaluating. Accounts for cold JVM startup (TLS handshake +
classloading). Default 30 was validated during live deploy-verify (Amendment 5).
initialDelaySeconds.title: initialDelaySeconds

reconcileIntervalSeconds.description:
reconcileIntervalSeconds: how often (in seconds) the registrar runs a full reconcile
pass to heal missed events or orphan entries. Set to 0 to disable periodic reconcile.
Disabling periodic reconciliation is NOT recommended.
reconcileIntervalSeconds.title: reconcileIntervalSeconds

watchNamespaces.description:
watchNamespaces: optional comma-separated list of namespaces for the registrar to watch.
When empty (default), the registrar watches all non-system namespaces — the correct
mode for multi-dataplane clusters where the registrar is shared across installs.
watchNamespaces.title: watchNamespaces

workloadSvidTTL.description: Optional per-entry TTL override for workload SPIRE entries (valkey, orchestrator, pep-server, inbound-worker, sink-agent, envoy). Defaults to 8h — shorter than agentSvidTTL (12h) so workload cert rotation is tightened out of the box, without affecting spire-agent's own node SVID lifetime or platform resilience to a spire-server outage. Set to "" to fall back to agentSvidTTL entirely, or to any other Go-duration string (minutes/hours only, greater than zero) to override the default.
workloadSvidTTL.title: workloadSvidTTL

annotations.description:
annotations — add the IRSA role ARN here when encryption.kms.type is aws.
IRSA lets the spire-server pod call AWS KMS without static credentials.
The IAM role must have KMS permissions.
Example:
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: "arn:aws:iam::ACCOUNT_ID:role/spire-server-kms"
annotations.title: annotations

automountServiceAccountToken.description:
Disable the default automounted token — the statefulset uses an explicit projected
token with a 1-hour expiry replacing the default unlimited token for k8s API calls.
automountServiceAccountToken.title: automountServiceAccountToken

upstreamAuthority.description:
upstreamAuthority controls whether SPIRE chains its CA to an external root CA.
When type is none (default), SPIRE is a self-signed root CA.
When set, SPIRE becomes an intermediate CA — its certificate is signed by the upstream.

type options:
  none:        SPIRE self-signed root CA. No external dependency. Default.
  disk:        Root CA cert + key loaded from a Kubernetes Secret mounted into the pod.
               The customer pre-creates the Secret. The chart mounts it read-only.
               Use for on-prem when an existing CA cert/key is available.
  certManager: SPIRE submits a CertificateRequest to cert-manager. cert-manager signs
               it using the configured Issuer. Requires cert-manager installed in cluster.
               Use for on-prem when cert-manager manages the customer PKI.
  awsPca:      SPIRE submits a CSR to AWS Private Certificate Authority.
               Requires IRSA and an existing ACM PCA. Use for AWS environments where
               the customer requires certs to chain to their AWS-native PKI.

secretName.description: Name of the Kubernetes Secret containing cert (tls.crt) and key (tls.key).

upstreamAuthority.title: upstreamAuthority

Matches the hardened defaults the dataplane components use.
securityContext.title: securityContext

socketHostPath.title: socketHostPath

socketPath.title: socketPath

volumeName.description: volumeName: Kubernetes volume name for the hostPath mount injected into dataplane pods.
volumeName.title: volumeName

waitInitContainer.description: waitInitContainer: gate dataplane Pod start until the agent socket is healthy.
waitInitContainer.title: waitInitContainer
